battle.title: Dining Philosophers Cage Match
battle.description: Bounded buffers, hungry readers and philosophers with too few forks.

questions.text: A bounded buffer uses semaphores empty (N), full (0) and mutex (1). A producer wrongly runs wait(mutex) BEFORE wait(empty). What can happen when the buffer is full?
options: The producer overwrites the oldest item
Deadlock: the producer holds the mutex while waiting for space, so no consumer can enter to free a slot
Nothing, the order of waits does not matter
The consumer produces the missing items itself
questions.answer: Deadlock: the producer holds the mutex while waiting for space, so no consumer can enter to free a slot
questions.explanation: The producer sleeps on empty while holding mutex, and a consumer needs mutex to remove an item and signal empty. The counting semaphore must be waited on first, then the mutex.

questions.text: In the classic readers-writers solution that gives readers priority, which problem can occur?
options: Two writers can write at the same time
Readers and a writer can read and write together
Writers can starve if readers keep arriving
questions.answer: Writers can starve if readers keep arriving
questions.explanation: New readers are admitted whenever any reader is active, so a waiting writer may never see the data unused. Mutual exclusion between writers and readers is still preserved.

questions.text: Which of these is NOT one of the four necessary conditions for deadlock?
questions.explanation: The condition is no preemption: a resource can be released only voluntarily by its holder. If resources could be taken away, deadlock could be broken, so preemption is the opposite of a requirement.

questions.text: Five philosophers each need forks i (left) and (i+1)%5 (right), but philosopher 4 picks fork 0 first and fork 4 second. Each first takes its first fork if free, then tries its second. How many philosophers eat after this single round?
questions.explanation: Philosophers 0 to 3 take forks 0 to 3, while philosopher 4 is blocked on fork 0. Only philosopher 3 finds its second fork (4) free, so one eats. Breaking the symmetry removes the circular wait.

questions.text: Five philosophers each grab the left fork and then wait for the right one, and the table deadlocks. Which fix is guaranteed to prevent deadlock?
options: Allow at most four philosophers to try to pick up forks at the same time
After a failed attempt, put the fork down and retry after a random delay
Give each philosopher a bigger plate
Add a sixth philosopher to the table
questions.answer: Allow at most four philosophers to try to pick up forks at the same time
questions.explanation: With at most 4 competing for 5 forks, at least one philosopher can always get both forks, so circular wait cannot form. Random back-off only makes deadlock unlikely and can livelock or starve someone.
